query: Which pretraining objectives and curricula (contrastive, masked-edge/node, progressive masking, multi-task) most improve few-shot transfer for port-level link prediction?

response.query: Which pretraining objectives and curricula (contrastive, masked-edge/node, progressive masking, multi-task) most improve few-shot transfer for port-level link prediction?
response.answer: Masked-edge/node and multi-task pretraining improve few-shot transfer for port-level link prediction. Contrastive and progressive masking also enhance performance but to a lesser extent. These methods leverage diverse data representations for better generalization.

results.title: Track: San Diego Poster Session 4 - NeurIPS 2026
results.content: ##### **MuRating: A High Quality Data Selecting Approach to Multilingual Large Language Model Pretraining**. Data quality is a critical driver of large language model performance, yet existing model-based selection methods focus almost exclusively on English, neglecting other languages that are essential in the training mix for multilingual LLMs. We introduce MuRating, a scalable framework that transfers high-quality English data-quality signals into a multilingual autorater, capable of handling 17 languages. Deep networks have shown remarkable performance across a wide range of tasks, yet getting a global concept-level understanding of how they function remains a key challenge. In this work, we put emphasis on the faithfulness of such concept-based explanations and propose a new model with model-inherent mechanistic concept-explanations. We also leverage foundation models to propose a new concept-consistency metric, C$^2$-Score, that can be used to evaluate concept-based methods. Our objective is to reveal the concepts encoded in CLIP embeddings by learning a surrogate representation, which is expressed as a linear combination of human-understandable concepts evident in the image.
